messages.subject: alignment of 3D ,meshes
parts:
Hello Dear all,

As many of you here, I am also new in R and have a basic question regarding Geomorph. I have 3-D meshes (ply files from micro-ct scans) of fish hearts and want to perform Procrustes analysis.

In order for the semi-landmarks to be located correctly via the digitsurface function, do I have to have the meshes aligned before introducing them into R?? Or the alignment on the XYZ axes will be done through the Procrustes??

Thanks a lot in advance,
Natasa

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] alignment of 3D ,meshes
parts:
Natasha,

 

Meshes do not need to be aligned prior to digitizing landmarks. The ‘digitsurface’ function should be able to accommodate reasonable differences in position and orientation.

 

Dean

Natasa

parts:
Dear Dean,

I am having some issues with the digitsurface function even though I took care of my meshes to be all with regularly spaced vertices. I have exported my fixed landmarks (n=7) from Amira (landmarkAscii format), and introduce them via a matrix format at the buildtemplate function producing 200 semilandmarks. 

I am attaching the code in  order for you to see if there are any mistakes: 

>scan130<-read.ply("E:/R file/scan130.ply", ShowSpecimen = TRUE, addNormals = FALSE)

>array_130<-read.amira.set ("E:/R file/scan130.landmarkAscii", 7)
>write.table(array_130,'fixed_130.nts')
>table130<-read.table('fixed_130.nts')
>matrix_130<-as.matrix(table130)
>plotspec(scan130, matrix_130, fixed = 7, ptsize = 1, centered = FALSE)
I have attached the image of the plotspec function.

> buildtemplate(scan130, matrix_130, 200, ptsize = 1, center = FALSE)
(see the picture)

> scan129<-read.ply("E:/R file/scan129_1500.ply", ShowSpecimen = TRUE, addNormals = FALSE)

>array_129<-read.amira.set ("E:/R file/scan129.landmarkAscii", 7)
>write.table(array_129, 'scan129.nts')
>table129<-read.table('scan129.nts')
>matrix_129<-as.matrix(table129)

>plotspec(scan129, matrix_129, fixed = 7, ptsize = 1, centered = FALSE)
(see picture)

and moving on to the digitsurface function which I need to ask if we put the fixed landmarks of the template or of the second specimen? In either way, the result is like the picture I have attached

> digitsurface(scan129, fixed=matrix_129, ptsize = 1, center = FALSE)

where the landmarks don't seem to be regulalry distributed.

The fixed landmarks at digitsurface function is logical to be the templates'? Since heart shape changes across specimens, don't I have to put the second specimens' fixed landmarks??

But again when I perform that, the result is the same with the picture attached.. Can you possibly figure out what is the problem??

Thank you in advance,
Natasa

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] alignment of 3D ,meshes
parts:
Natasa,

 

Yes, digitizing from 3D surfaces is challenging. Admitedly, the digitsurface function is somewhat limited in its capabilities. I did notice though that you have center = FALSE.  You might change that to TRUE to see whether you can better manipulate things.

 

If not, you may need to digitize in another package first.

Dean
